newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-ZILE REFUSED MERRILL OFFER ON EUROBOND, T-BILLS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-ZILE REFUSED MERRILL OFFER ON EUROBOND, T-BILLS.

text.p: Latvia refused an offer from investment house Merrill Lynch to issue eurobonds worth $200 million and Merrill's offer to buy all of a planned issue of two-year T-bills, Finance Minister Robert Zile said on Thursday.
"Merrill Lynch offered to issue government securities on the international market worth $200 million and lengthen the maturity of our total debt market to 20 years," Zile told a news conference.
"We refused the offer as we need to maintain the local debt market," Zile said.
He said Merrill made the offer while he was in London for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) annual meeting.
Zile also said that Merrill approached Latvia two months ago to underwrite the whole of a planned two-year T-bill issue but the offer was refused as issuing domestically was better.
"The result in an auction would be better than the one offered by Merrill when under-writing the whole issue," he said.
Zile also said the majority of companies he met were offering either credit lines against state guarantees or were ready to issue eurobonds of a mininum $100 million.
"We invited the companies to invest in private projects, had talks on issues like housing projects...Liepaja harbour," he said.
